intro.title: Build refresh token rotation flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure refresh token rotation flow for a Node.js application. You will learn how to automatically issue new access tokens using a refresh token when the old one expires, enhancing security by reducing token reuse. The core programming concepts involve managing JWT (JSON Web Token) validation, state handling for tokens, and implementing conditional logic for token refresh. You will work with JavaScript, the jsonwebtoken library, and HTTP headers to handle authentication tokens. By the end, you'll have a functional flow that rotates tokens to keep user sessions secure without requiring frequent logins.
intro.usecase: Refresh token rotation is a critical security pattern used in virtually every modern web application that maintains user sessions. When you stay logged into platforms like Gmail, Netflix, or banking dashboards for extended periods, your access tokens expire periodically, but the app seamlessly refreshes them in the background without requiring you to re-enter credentials. This flow ensures continuous, secure access in admin panels, e-commerce platforms, and collaborative tools where users interact with data-rich interfaces for hours. As a Node.js developer, implementing this properly prevents session hijacking while delivering the smooth, uninterrupted experience users expect from professional applications.
